summary: XRD analysis across the paper focuses on the effect of varying CsBr/KBr treatment on CsPbBr3 quantum dot films. All samples, including pristine and treated films, exhibit a main diffraction peak at 21.5° 2θ. With increasing CsBr/KBr content, the peak intensity increases and the peak position shifts slightly to higher 2θ, suggesting changes in crystallinity or lattice contraction. However, quantitative details such as FWHM and phase identification are not provided, limiting the depth of structural interpretation.

key_findings.finding: All CsPbBr3 QD films, regardless of CsBr/KBr treatment, show a main XRD peak at 21.5° 2θ.
With increasing CsBr/KBr treatment, the XRD peak intensity increases and the peak position shifts slightly to higher 2θ.

scientific_interpretation.claim: The increase in XRD peak intensity with higher CsBr/KBr treatment suggests improved crystallinity or increased grain size in CsPbBr3 QD films.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: The trend of increasing peak intensity with treatment is commonly associated with enhanced crystallinity or larger coherent domain size, as indicated by the analysis trend.

citations.evidence: peak intensity increases with CsBr/KBr treatment

scientific_interpretation.claim: The slight shift of the main XRD peak to higher 2θ with increasing CsBr/KBr content may indicate a reduction in lattice parameter, possibly due to incorporation of smaller ions or lattice contraction.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: A shift to higher 2θ typically corresponds to a decrease in d-spacing, which can result from lattice contraction or compositional changes.

citations.evidence: peak position shifts slightly to higher 2θ with increasing CsBr/KBr

scientific_interpretation.claim: No new crystalline phases are detected upon CsBr/KBr treatment, as all samples show only the main peak at 21.5° 2θ.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: The absence of additional peaks across all conditions suggests phase purity is maintained.

citations.evidence: All conditions list only a peak at 21.5

limitations.claim: No quantitative peak width (FWHM) data is provided, limiting the ability to assess crystallite size or microstrain.
No explicit phase identification or lattice parameter calculation is reported, so phase assignment and structural changes are inferred rather than confirmed.
Only one XRD figure is available, so cross-figure structural trends cannot be established beyond the single dataset.
